Alright guys! Welcome to the beginner tank recommendation megathread! First, I would like to clarify what qualifies as a beginner tank. Beginner tanks means no subtanks like the Kanger Subtanks, Aspire Atlantis, eGo One, and so forth. They have their own thread.

The Rules

All parent comments must be in the following format:

 Manufacturer |Tank Name |Price Range |Review Link
---------|----------

* Discussions on why you personally recommend it

So it ends up looking like:

House of Hybrids Kabuki Tank $89.99 Review

Moderator's note: I used an ECF link above, because the one YouTube video I could find on it had little to no useful information, and the thread within the first three pages has more pictures than the video review did. This will be acceptable if no review or trustworthy reviews have been posted. Trustworthiness of reviews will be decided by the mods.

  • I would recommend the Kabuki tank because House of Hybrids are known for their quality work, they have a great warranty on their devices (outside of things like glass). The Aspire Nautilus coils use Japanese cotton, widely available, and come in a temperature control variety. Furthermore, the Kabuki Tank holds 3mL of liquid, is smaller than regular Nautilus tanks, and has much more precise airflow control. Though they are expensive, if you can spare the scratch, House of Hybrids is worth it.

Any questions, additional reviews or information regarding the tanks should take place in response to the parent comment.

All discussions of sales, additional reviews, pricing, etc. will be posted in response to the original piece of gear. Double posts will be deleted.

Feel free to link to reviews that have been posted on /v/vaping already as part of the post.

Rules will be updated as needed.

But /u/NewFatMike, why is this thing?

Until we have a wiki capacity, this will be a useful tool to come to for new gear reviews. Furthermore, it will be good to have a running record of what gear is out there. This thread will be useful because it will let us see more novel and new gear for the people who want to see it and provide a wealth of information for people coming in late to learn everything they want in discussion about the piece of gear in question.

Go forth, vaping lovelies, and recommend!

Aspire Nautilus Mini $30 - $35 Review
  • Notes: Decent vape with an abundance of gizmos and toys to make your life easier. Metal sleeved tank replacements are a must if you've got butterfingers! Coils last longer than any BVC/BDC out there, producing clean, thick vape that satisfies. Aspire BVC / BDC $6 - $10 Review
  • Notes: Abundant! These are everywhere, from gas stations to vape shops to about every place you can look online. Cheap cheap cheap is the name of the game here, coil heads are cheap as well - because of this product's age. Not for getting super lung hits or blasting fat clouds out into the room, but it should be enough to get even the two, three pack a day smoker to make the switch.

Anyvape Davide (Aspire and/or Kanger vers.) $10 - $15 Review 1 Review 2
  • Notes: This beautiful tank comes in two varieties - Aspire and Kanger. I heavily recommend the Aspire version. That version doesn't cost you very much more (maybe a dollar or two) and comes with two additional pieces- a spacer ring and a white plastic grommet that closes off the juice feed a little to accomodate the Aspire BVC coil heads. Assemble it without that spacer and grommet and throw an older, single coil Kanger head in there and it'll work just fine. With the bigger Kanger dual coil heads, use the spacer ring and not the grommet and you're still working. I considered this thing the Swiss Army Knife of beginner tanks, and used it for a very, very long time. Much bigger tank capacity than anything else that was out that didn't have 'Protank' printed on it.

Kangertech Aerotank $20 - $25 Review
  • Notes: Kangertech's venture into increased airflow and bigger, more impressive vapor production started with this guy. It's satisfying and functional, coil heads aren't going to break your wallet, and it holds a substantial amount of juice. If you need to feel a little less like you're sucking a milkshake through a straw, this one's got an adjustable airflow and it's probably your best bet.

Somewhat unrelated question: if I was interested in learning more about the market for gold, silver, platinum, etc. how would you advise that I go about doing that? How did you get involved?

I started buying silver as sort of an anti-hobby.

I'm one of those people who jumps from hobby to hobby every few months, and in the process, spends a bunch of money. In an effort to curb my nonstop buying of electronics, guitars, tools and other things that I lose interest in, I started buying silver, with the rationale that there was a lot to learn about the precious metals market (both historically and financially) so it would take me a while to run out of things to read/learn/discuss, and that when I did eventually get bored, I could just sell my stack, something that I couldn't do with my other hobbies.

So, I started reading websites, visiting discussion forums and watching videos, and eventually bought a few ounces of silver online. That was almost three years ago, and I've been going strong on silver (and to a lesser degree gold) ever since. I still blow my money as soon as I get it, but now my purchases take the form of silver in my safe.

To answer your question more directly, start thinking about why you want to invest in precious metals. That will guide you as you decide what to buy. At the same time, start reading articles from the web, and visiting forums. Honestly, the Silverbugs community over at Reddit is extremely helpful and knowledgeable. Spend some time reading postings over there, and the ones in this subverse, and ask questions when you have them. Pretty soon, you'll know if you want to get in, or not.

The first and most important advice I can give you is: do your own research.

I'm a young guy and so I am finding my place in adult life, slowly getting tuned into the financial and political world. In some ways, 'waking up' as an adult after the 2008 recession has been a blessing.

One thing I have discovered, nearly all financial advice pre-2008 is wrong now. Or obsolete. I'm not sure what dark magic they did, but the precious metals markets have been stable for a long time. WWI and WWII went by without nearly a blip, but then in the decade 2001–2008 there was a huge run up, and then since 2008 all of the markets have just gone sideways. Nothing is following any previous pattern right now. Will things return to how they were pre-2001? It doesn't feel like it. Will things continue this weird sidetrack we've been doing since 2008? It seems likely for at least the near-future. But from where I stand, with massive debt in the US (and Puerto Rico) and potential collapse of Greece and maybe the Euro, I'm not sure that things are going to get better before they get a little more crazy.

Standing here in 2015 it sure feels like we're in for a wild ride in the next few years!

Keep this in mind whenever somebody says "Precious Metals will be sacred during times of financial crisis" or "When the dollar is unstable, precious metals will be worth more".

If you look at the last 15 years. Silver has a long way to go down before it is really low. If you look at the past 3 years it's doing just fine. My advice is: if you're in silver for the long term (more than 5 years) buy while the price dips, and sit tight on your stack when the price rises and be happy :)

If I wasn't just laid off two weeks ago I'd be buying silver up. Sadly I've sold off most of my stack to fund a larger investment. :(
